info.description: Keys, webhooks, usage and SSO connections. Auth is a workspace key in `Authorization: Bearer ab_live_…` or `x-api-key`; only its hash is stored.

post.summary: Mint a key; the plaintext is returned once
post.description: `scopes` may be omitted, and then the new key inherits the scopes of the key that minted it. It used to inherit `*` instead, so a caller holding only `keys:write` could mint a key holding everything. A `scopes` that is sent must be a non-empty list of the names below, an unknown member is refused by name rather than filtered out, and a known one the calling key does not itself hold is a 403 — a key may hand out its own authority and no more. Re-scoping an existing key (`PATCH /api/keys/{id}`) follows the same rule.

400.description: Body is not a JSON object

403.description: Needs keys:write, or asks for a scope the calling key does not hold

409.description: This workspace already has 20 live keys

422.description: A field was refused; see error.fields

patch.summary: Rename, re-scope or re-limit a key
patch.description: Names at least one field: an empty body is refused rather than answered with the row it left untouched. Fields this route does not own (`revokedAt`, `hashedKey`) are not accepted — revoking is DELETE. `scopes` is checked against the key making the call, because re-scoping is granting: a key may set only scopes it holds, and `*` is a scope.

400.description: Body is not a JSON object

403.description: Needs keys:write, or asks for a scope the calling key does not hold

post.summary: Receive a signed NuCRM webhook and publish it to matching subscriptions
post.description: This is the address a NuCRM integration webhook posts to — the receiving end of the bridge, where `POST /api/v1/events` is the publishing end your own code calls. Create a source in the dashboard (Connect NuCRM), then configure the NuCRM integration with this URL, `Authorization: Bearer <key>` plus the integration's secret. The body is NuCRM's envelope; `x-nucrm-signature` is `sha256=` + HMAC-SHA256 of the exact bytes, keyed by the source's secret (the `sha256=` prefix is optional and both spellings verify). `x-nucrm-delivery` deduplicates NuCRM's own retries: a repeat answers `200` with `duplicate: true` and publishes nothing. An accepted event gets one Delivery per matching subscription, counted like `POST /api/v1/events`; a paused source answers 409 and NuCRM parks the delivery after its five attempts.

parameters.name: x-nucrm-signature
parameters.description: HMAC-SHA256 of the request body, hex, optionally prefixed `sha256=`.

parameters.name: x-nucrm-delivery
parameters.description: NuCRM's delivery id. A repeat of one already accepted answers 200 with `duplicate: true`.

timestamp.description: NuCRM's ISO moment. Declared, not interpreted — deliveries carry their own.

data.description: The payload every matching subscriber receives, signed. Omit it for none; `null` is refused.

200.description: Duplicate delivery: already accepted, nothing published again

202.description: Accepted — one Delivery per matching subscription (same receipt as POST /api/v1/events)

400.description: Body is not a JSON object

401.description: No key, or x-nucrm-signature missing/does not match the source's secret

404.description: No such inbound source in this workspace

get.description: Each delivery carries its status (PENDING, DELIVERED, RETRYING, DEAD), attempt log, and nextAttemptAt when a retry is scheduled.

post.summary: Re-send one delivery, or every dead one
post.description: Copies the stored payload into a NEW delivery so the failed original stays on the record. Refused while the endpoint is disabled. Retries are at-least-once, so a receiver must dedupe on the x-abetapi-delivery header.

requestBody.description: Either `deliveryId`, or `all: true` with an optional `status` (defaults to DEAD). A boolean is a boolean: `all: "yes"` used to be answered as though `deliveryId` were the missing field.

post.summary: Explain a webhook's recent delivery failures
post.description: Read-only and workspace-scoped: it selects no `secretHash` and retries nothing. A signed-in dashboard session is accepted as well as a key. Its refusals for a wrong field are this document's own envelope; the 404 below is not, and is described as it actually answers.

200.description: A diagnosis, or an honest "nothing to diagnose" with the stats beside it

400.description: Body is not a JSON object

404.description: No such webhook in this workspace. This answer is `{ error: "webhook not found" }` — a bare string, not the envelope above — because the app's own dashboard prints it: `ai-panel.tsx` renders `data.error` as text. Documented rather than quietly different.

502.description: The model was unreachable; delivery records are unaffected
